headline: 483 g/t Au UNDERGROUND — Cambria Gold's First Premier Infill Holes Hit 19.82 g/t Over 5.0m at Historic BC Gold Mine
snippet: Cambria Gold Mines (TSX-V: CAMB) reported first results from its underground infill drill program at the Prew Zone of the Premier Gold Project in northwestern British Columbia, returning 19.82 g/t Au over 5.0 metres (including 45.88 g/t over 2.0m), with a standout 483.0 g/t Au over 1.0 metre in hole P26U-0003. The delineation program uses tightly spaced 12.5-metre drill centres from underground platforms; tight assay spacings at these grades — in a historically significant BC gold camp currently being evaluated for restart — support a high-confidence near-surface resource model for mine planning.

headline: CAMECO JV SUMMER DRILL UNDERWAY — CanAlaska Launches $15M West McArthur Pike Zone Step-Out Campaign in Athabasca Basin
snippet: CanAlaska Uranium Ltd. (TSX-V: CVV) announced the start of its summer 2026 drill campaign at the West McArthur Joint Venture in the southeastern Athabasca Basin, co-funded with Cameco Corporation under the JV where CanAlaska holds 88.89%. The $15 million program focuses on step-outs to the northeast and southwest of the Pike Zone's defined high-grade footprint to evaluate whether 2025-discovered mineralization continues along strike; results are expected before September completion, and Cameco's co-funding signals institutional confidence in the target's potential inside the world's premier uranium district.

headline: 25,000 METRES IN MOTION — Sirios Resources Deploys 2 Rigs at Cheechoo Quebec Gold, Targeting 2027 Resource Update + PEA
snippet: Sirios Resources Inc. (TSX-V: SOI) confirmed all required permits are received and the first two of three planned drill rigs are now active at the Cheechoo Gold Project in Eeyou Istchee, Quebec — the largest-known gold project in the James Bay region by deposit footprint. Phase 1 of the fully funded 25,000m program is designed to support an updated NI 43-101 mineral resource estimate underpinning a Preliminary Economic Assessment planned for H1 2027; a third rig joins at end of June and a LIBS laser spectrometry unit is deployed for real-time on-site core analysis, making this one of the most active junior drill campaigns in Canada this summer.

headline: TWO DRILLS ON SITE — Trident Resources Mobilizes at Contact Lake for 20,000m Saskatchewan Gold Summer Campaign
snippet: Trident Resources Corp. (TSX-V: TTD) confirmed all geological personnel and two drill rigs are now on-site at the Contact Lake Gold Project in Saskatchewan, launching a 2026 summer program of over 20,000 metres in approximately 35 holes running through November. The campaign follows the company's strongest intercept to date — 17.88 g/t Au over 11.25 metres including 42.53 g/t over 4.50m from just 86 metres depth (May 27) — and targets expansion of that high-grade system along strike and at depth, where open mineralization could significantly grow the project resource base.

headline: HAT COPPER-GOLD GROWS EAST 150M — Doubleview Opens 'Far East Zone' With 8.0m at 4.04 g/t Au Outside Existing PEA Pit Shell
snippet: Doubleview Gold Corp. (TSX-V: DBG) reported assay results from holes H102-H108 at its Hat copper-gold porphyry project in northwestern British Columbia that extend known mineralization approximately 150 metres beyond the 2026 PEA pit boundary, establishing a new 'Far East Zone.' The headline intercept of 8.0 metres grading 4.04 g/t Au (with 112.0m at 0.40 g/t Au in a broader envelope) adds a gold-enriched satellite target to the flanks of the existing bulk-tonnage resource; these holes were not incorporated into the February 2026 MRE or March 2026 PEA, and follow-up drilling is required to determine geometry and continuity.

headline: ROSE WEST SUMMER DRILL LAUNCHED — Critical Elements Deploys 2 Rigs in 10,000m Quebec Lithium Footprint Expansion
snippet: Critical Elements Lithium Corporation (TSX-V: CRE) announced commencement of its 10,000-metre Summer 2026 drill program at the Rose West Discovery in Eeyou Istchee, Quebec, deploying two rigs to expand a lithium-tantalum pegmatite system already grown from 450m × 370m to 1,250m × 800m during Winter 2026 drilling. The program targets lateral expansion, infill of Line C for grade continuity, and follow-up on newly discovered pegmatites 6 and 7 below current depth limits; Rose is the most advanced hardrock lithium project in Eastern Canada, with a completed feasibility study, Cree community agreement, road access, and proximity to hydroelectric power.

headline: UEC SELLS ZERO URANIUM IN Q3 — $0 Revenue vs $8.5M Estimate, But Burke Hollow ISR Starts; $794M Liquidity, No Debt
snippet: Uranium Energy Corp. (NYSE American: UEC) reported fiscal Q3 2026 actual results with revenue of $0 — well below the $8.5 million analyst consensus — after no uranium was sold in the quarter ended April 30; the company produced 32,195 lbs of U₃O₈ at a cash cost of $46.69/lb and held inventory rather than selling at prevailing spot prices. The key operational catalyst is that production has commenced at Burke Hollow, UEC's third ISR uranium mine in South Texas, expanding its active platform; total liquid assets of $794 million ($488M cash, no debt) and 1.456 million lbs of U₃O₈ inventory at $127M market value confirm the company is positioned to choose its timing on future sales.

headline: BERTHA NORTH DRILL COMMENCES — Torr Metals' 6,000m Copper-Gold Porphyry Program Targets 800×500m Anomaly; 2.4% Cu Grab Samples
snippet: Torr Metals Inc. (TSX-V: TMET) announced the commencement of its fully funded 6,000-metre Phase II drill program at the Bertha North copper-gold porphyry target in British Columbia, following surface rock samples returning up to 2.4% copper and 9.4 g/t silver from potassically altered brecciated intrusive float. Integrated geophysical surveys define a large undrilled porphyry core with a magnetic-resistive centre flanked by strengthening chargeability-conductivity responses at depth — a signature interpreted as analogous to the upper alteration profile of the New Afton copper-gold deposit; an 800m × 500m coincident copper-gold soil anomaly directly overlies the target.

headline: GDXJ DOWN 10.8% YTD, BUT HISTORY SAYS BUY — Gold 200-Day MA Breaks Average +3.5% Six-Month Return; Miners Lag Then Outperform
snippet: Benzinga analysis using VanEck data finds that across the last 10 instances of gold falling below its 200-day moving average, the average one-month return is essentially flat (−0.15%) but the average six-month return is +3.5%, suggesting the June 8 200-day break — the first since October 2023 — is historically a buying opportunity rather than a trend-reversal signal. The VanEck Junior Gold Miners ETF (GDXJ) was off 10.8% year-to-date as of June 5, deepening the disconnect between miner valuations and still-elevated gold prices; that gap has historically preceded the sharpest phases of miner outperformance relative to bullion in subsequent cycles.

headline: GOLD BELOW 200 EMA FOR FIRST TIME SINCE OCTOBER 2023 — $4,280 Is Last Defence Before -20% Bear Case Target Opens
snippet: Finance Magnates documents gold's technical breakdown following the May payrolls shock: a close below the 200-day EMA at $4,370 on June 8 — the first since October 2023 — leaves bullion 23% below the January 29 all-time high of $5,595.  The structural bear scenario requires a weekly close below $4,280 (the October 2025 resistance-turned-support level), which would open a measured-move target around $3,440; the bull case requires a decisive reclaim of $4,370 before Wednesday's CPI print, which remains possible if May inflation comes in below the expected 4.2% consensus.
